attributes.collision_incidents: TWO adopted candidates were reverted after the post-rename full ninja build failed with mwld 'multiply-defined' link errors: (1) fn_8009FCA8->DoAudioTallySFX collided with a pre-existing genuine DoAudioTallySFX at a different address (0x8009FB84) in the same TU; (2) AudioPlayerPoison->AudioPlayerSeverePain collided with a pre-existing genuine AudioPlayerSeverePain at a different address (0x8009F7D8) in the same TU, and a caller in gauntworld.c ('if (amt < sZeroDouble) { ... AudioPlayerPoison(a->index); }', a negative-amount/poison-item pickup handler) further confirmed the original name's semantics were already correct. Both reverts were verified clean (symbols.txt line-by-line diff, no old-name leakage anywhere in src/include/symbols.txt) before the final green build. Full writeup and the generalizable lesson: claim.law.symaudit-candidate-collision-risk.20260831.v1.
attributes.gate_method: Batch rename executed via one Python script (whole-word regex substitution across config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt + all src/**/*.c,*.h + include/**/*.c,*.h) rather than 24 individual edits, to keep the reference-propagation exhaustive and auditable. After the batch: grepped build/GUNE5D/**/*.s and obj/**/*.o for every old name (60 stale generated files found and deleted across 18 affected TUs' splits/objects), python configure.py, ninja -j2 -> full green with build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK and progress IDENTICAL to the pre-rename baseline (97.84% fuzzy / 58.15% matched / 26.09% linked, Game Code 97.33%/48.27%/8.64% -- both measured via python configure.py progress equivalent baked into the ninja PROGRESS step). Spot-checked fndiff --clean on 5 renamed functions across 5 different TUs (StdCamReturn: MATCH pool-noise-only; enemy_update: EXACT; StartGenHitFx: SCHEDULE_CANDIDATE 6 real diff lines, IDENTICAL residual to its pre-rename park; setChrome: MATCH pool-noise-only; AudioGeneratorDies: EXACT) -- zero regression, confirming the whole batch is codegen-neutral as expected for pure identifier renames. git diff --check passed (no whitespace errors); diff stat is a clean 162 insertions / 162 deletions across 17 files (pure substitution, no incidental changes).
attributes.graph_repair: The rename broke `gdlmem.py build` project-wide ('record references unknown entity function:fn_80089350') because 4 pre-existing accepted attempt records anchored their required `function` field to an OLD fn_ name that no longer resolves against the post-rename symbols.txt: attempt.fn-80089350-portable-closure.20260829.v1 (function:fn_80089350 -> function:PlyrSfxDoDamage, plus its attributes.anchors example-command text updated to match), attempt.parked.fn_80091ac0.20260829.v1 (-> function:StartGenHitFx), attempt.parked.fn_800920e0.20260829.v1 (-> function:StartBagFX), attempt.parked.pbsetdodrawregs.20260829.v1 (-> function:setTexInfo). These were repaired as narrow in-place pointer fixes (content/finding unchanged, only the anchor updated) rather than as content supersessions, because attempt-record versioning does not exempt superseded copies from entity-resolution validation -- a v2-with-supersedes would NOT have fixed the build. `gdlmem.py build` was re-run and confirmed clean (attempt count unchanged at 384, no records lost) and `gdlmem.py context <new-name>` was spot-checked for all 4 to confirm the historical park/improvement records still surface correctly. Full writeup and the generalizable lesson: claim.law.symbol-rename-orphans-attempt-records.20260831.v1.
attributes.law_screen: claim.law.cross-tu-symbol-rename: APPLIED throughout -- every rename was propagated via grep of every src/**/*.c,*.h reference (including cross-TU extern decls/call sites in sibling-owned files: bosscam.c, gamemain.c, critter.c, tower.c, auxscreen.c, shop.c, gauntworld.c, player.c, combat.c, pmotion.c), stale build/GUNE5D/asm/**/*.s and obj/**/*.o for every renamed symbol were identified and deleted, and python configure.py was re-run before rebuilding; a green ninja after a prior failed one was never treated as sufficient (two real build failures this pass -- see below -- were both diagnosed from a full ninja run, not skipped). claim.law.walked-base-symbol-identity / claim.law.gcb-sflags-relocation-alias / claim.law.bss-reverse-declaration-order: screened (symbol-identity tag), none applicable -- this pass only renamed existing function identifiers (pure text substitution across all references), never introduced a new raw-offset conversion, alias, or BSS declaration that any of these three govern. claim.law.symaudit-candidate-collision-risk and claim.law.symbol-rename-orphans-attempt-records: NEW laws proposed this pass (see accompanying records) documenting two build-breaking hazard classes discovered live during execution (name collision with an existing same-TU symbol; orphaned attempt-record function anchors) -- both are now first-class screening items for any future rename pass.

TOTALS across all 7 TUs: 38 candidates screened, 24 adopted (renamed), 8 rejected (documented), 6 deferred (documented).
attributes.verification_method: Per candidate: python tools/gdl/fnasm.py <unit> <fn> for target disassembly where relevant, Read of the full function body plus its callers (grep -rn across src/), and cross-referencing any pre-existing in-source doc comments (several TUs already carried partial Xbox-candidate guesses or behavioral analysis comments from earlier sessions, which either corroborated or -- in one case, pb_objregs.c's fn_800C6350 -- were themselves superseded by this pass' more specific evidence and corrected in-source). Rejections and deferrals were reached on POSITIVE contradicting or ambiguous evidence, never on absence of evidence alone, except where an explicit prior in-source safety constraint (pb_frame.c) made an empirical test too risky to justify for 4 renames.
